entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-w5f2-9q9c-ff4h: LMCache: Remote code execution via unsafe deserialization in multiprocess mode transport
entry.content:
LMCache: Remote code execution via unsafe deserialization in multiprocess mode transport

Aliases: CVE-2026-105192

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • lmcache — fixed in 0.5.6

### Summary LMCache is vulnerable to Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via Pickle Deserialization on the Multiprocess ZMQ Transport ### Details LMCache multiprocess mode, also called distributed mode, opens an unauthenticated ZeroMQ ROUTER so worker processes can register and share KV cache blocks. The intended clients are sibling LMCache processes. There is no CURVE, ZAP, password, or message authentication on that socket. LMCache used only inside a vLLM process does not open this port. The transport binds to localhost unless the operator sets a routable address with --host, which is how multi-node deployments let peers connect. The 9.8 score is for that routable configuration. A stock single-host install that leaves the default bind is not reachable from other machines. Message…

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-h4mw-j7qp-8mwm: Claude Agent SDK: Argument Injection via resume Option Allows Arbitrary Command Execution
entry.content:
Claude Agent SDK: Argument Injection via resume Option Allows Arbitrary Command Execution

Aliases: CVE-2026-96620

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • claude-agent-sdk — fixed in 0.2.121

The Claude Agent SDK for Python passed the `resume` option to the Claude CLI without validation, allowing a value beginning with `-` to be interpreted as a separate CLI flag. An attacker who controlled the `resume` value could inject an `--mcp-config` flag defining a stdio MCP server, resulting in arbitrary command execution at CLI startup that bypassed the SDK's permission controls. Exploitation required an application to pass untrusted input as the session ID to resume. Users are advised to update to the latest version of the claude-agent-sdk package. Thank you to hackerone.com/moamenmahmood for reporting this issue.

References:

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-vgf9-9mxx-hq54: ClickMigrate has Path Traversal in "revision -m" argument
entry.content:
ClickMigrate has Path Traversal in "revision -m" argument

Aliases: CVE-2026-68549

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N

Affected:

  • clickmigrate — fixed in 1.0.3

### Impact A path traversal vulnerability in the `revision` command allowed a crafted migration name supplied via the `-m` argument to escape the intended migrations directory. Under specific conditions, an attacker could cause the tool to create a `.sql` file in an arbitrary location writable by the user executing the command. This issue is only exploitable if an attacker can influence the migration name passed to the `revision` command, such as through an insecure automation or CI/CD pipeline that forwards untrusted input. ### Patches The vulnerability has been fixed in version 1.0.3 by validating and sanitizing the migration name to prevent directory traversal. Users should upgrade to version 1.0.3 or later. ### Workarounds Do not pass untrusted input to the `revision -m` argument.…

entry.title: [NEW] MAL-2026-17866: Malicious code in pyyi (PyPI)
entry.content:
Malicious code in pyyi (PyPI)

Affected:

  • pyyi

The verified PyPI wheel declares a console command named python2 (pyyi.cli:main). For commands other than the local REPL, help, version, unlock, or uninstall paths, it obtains configuration and calls run_payload(). Registration sends the hostname and OS to a configured space-z.ai server and stores the returned apiKey in ~/.python2/config.json. The REPL presents a normal Python banner but silently sends eligible single-token inputs to /api/cli/unlock as the password field, subject to filtering and attempt limits. run_payload() fetches code from /api/cli/payload, base64-decodes and gzip-decompresses it, then executes it in memory using exec(compile(src, '<adv>', 'exec'), g) at pyyi/cli.py:640 and calls its main function. Loader failures are disguised as Python's can't open file error. The ma…

entry.title: [UPDATED] PYSEC-2026-2946: PraisonAI: Coarse-Grained Tool Approval Cache Bypasses Per-Invocation Consent for Shell Commands
entry.content:
PraisonAI: Coarse-Grained Tool Approval Cache Bypasses Per-Invocation Consent for Shell Commands

Aliases: CVE-2026-56074, GHSA-ffp3-3562-8cv3

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • praisonaiagents — fixed in 4.5.128

## Summary The approval system in PraisonAI Agents caches tool approval decisions by tool name only, not by invocation arguments. Once a user approves `execute_command` for any command (e.g., `ls -la`), all subsequent `execute_command` calls in that execution context bypass the approval prompt entirely. Combined with `os.environ.copy()` passing all process environment variables to subprocesses, this allows an LLM agent (potentially via prompt injection) to silently exfiltrate API keys and credentials without further user consent. ## Details The `require_approval` decorator in `src/praisonai-agents/praisonaiagents/approval/__init__.py:176-178` checks approval status by tool name only: ```python @wraps(func) def wrapper(*args, **kwargs): if is_already_approved(tool_name): # line 17…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-5wp5-5229-5g6q: NLTK: Missing Post-Download Integrity Verification Allows Malicious Package Injection
entry.content:
NLTK: Missing Post-Download Integrity Verification Allows Malicious Package Injection

Aliases: CVE-2026-12259, CVE-2026-63310, GHSA-gf32-cmjh-8m9v, PYSEC-2026-3729, PYSEC-2026-4318

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • nltk — fixed in 3.9.3

NLTK's package downloader in nltk/downloader.py does not verify file integrity after download and before extraction. The download flow at lines 789-825: 1. File is downloaded to a temp path via HTTP 2. os.replace(tmp_filepath, filepath) moves it to the final location (line 799) 3. Extraction begins via _unzip_iter() (line 825) Between steps 2 and 3, there is no SHA-256 verification. The checksum logic exists in _pkg_status() (lines 982-1015) but it is only used BEFORE download as a status check ("is this package already installed and up-to-date?"). It is never called after download to verify the file that was actually received. Attack vectors: 1. MITM during HTTP download (NLTK downloads from http:// by default on some mirrors) 2. Race condition on shared filesystems (attacker replaces …

entry.title: [UPDATED] PYSEC-2026-4318: In nltk version 3.9.4, the `nltk.downloader.Downloader._download_package()` function writes downloaded package bytes to
entry.content:
Aliases: CVE-2026-12259, CVE-2026-63310, GHSA-5wp5-5229-5g6q, GHSA-gf32-cmjh-8m9v, PYSEC-2026-3729

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • nltk

In nltk version 3.9.4, the `nltk.downloader.Downloader._download_package()` function writes downloaded package bytes to disk and may extract them before enforcing SHA-256 or MD5 checksum validation. This allows an attacker to tamper with the package response body for `info.url` through a compromised mirror, malicious proxy, or other source-substitution condition, leading to the installation of attacker-controlled package bytes. The vulnerability can result in malicious corpus or model content being trusted by downstream users or applications.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-cjg8-h5qc-hrjv: kedro-datasets has a path traversal vulnerability in PartitionedDataset that allows arbitrary file write
entry.content:
kedro-datasets has a path traversal vulnerability in PartitionedDataset that allows arbitrary file write

Aliases: CVE-2026-111170, CVE-2026-35492, PYSEC-2026-2545

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • kedro-datasets — fixed in 9.3.0

### Impact PartitionedDataset in kedro-datasets was vulnerable to path traversal. Partition IDs were concatenated directly with the dataset base path without validation. An attacker or malicious input containing .. components in a partition ID could cause files to be written outside the configured dataset directory, potentially overwriting arbitrary files on the filesystem. Users of PartitionedDataset with any storage backend (local filesystem, S3, GCS, etc.) are affected. ### Patches Yes. The vulnerability has been patched in kedro-datasets version 9.3.0. Users should upgrade to kedro-datasets >= 9.3.0. The fix normalizes constructed paths using `posixpath.normpath` and validates that the resolved path remains within the dataset base directory before use, raising a `DatasetError` if the…

## Summary web3.py implements CCIP Read / `OffchainLookup` (EIP-3668) by performing HTTP requests to URLs supplied by smart contracts in `offchain_lookup_payload["urls"]`. The implementation uses these contract-supplied URLs directly (after `{sender}` / `{data}` template substitution) without any destination validation: - No restriction to `https://` (and no opt-in gate for `http://`) - No hostname or IP allowlist - No blocking of private/reserved IP ranges (loopback, link-local, RFC1918) - No redirect target validation (both `requests` and `aiohttp` follow redirects by default) **CCIP Read is enabled by default** (`global_ccip_read_enabled = True` on all providers), meaning any application using web3.py's `.call()` method is exposed without explicit opt-in. entry.content:
Malicious code in py-worm (PyPI)

Affected:

  • py-worm

Importing py-worm's `agentaix` module downloads a mutable Python file from `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anonrider404/pypl/refs/heads/main/readme.txt` to a temporary `.py` file and launches it without a visible console on Windows. Versions 0.1.0 and 2.0.0 do this directly during import; version 2.0.1 starts a daemon thread during import to perform the same action. The package's CLI and GUI entry points import this module.
